title: ci(ui-merge): `Type Check UI` is red on every PR whose ui affected-scope is empty — `type-check:vitest-setup` compiles against unbuilt `@object-ui/*` dists after turbo built nothing (bill item 49)
body:
Filing gate ① (CI gate false-red, reach: PR runs on `main`) + ④: aftercare of the cutover #25752 (`pm:epic`; epic PM `session_01RSDL3SFtJaKzcymvCD8RsU`). Part of #25677. Touches `.github/workflows/ci.yml` = Tier H: GOVERNED_APPROVERS review, the PR stops at draft.

**谁付代价（业务筛）:** the maintainer wants `Type Check UI` in the required set (procedure #25752 step 6) and it was held back at the sitting only because of this red (ruling: add `Lint UI` + `Build & E2E UI` now, `Type Check UI` after the fix). Until then a spec change that breaks the Console compile is caught only by `Build & E2E UI`, and every workflow-only or root-only PR that touches a `ui_consumers` path shows a red check that means nothing.

## Measured

- PR B #25827 head `f973a4f3fd` (workflow + scripts diff, no `ui/` change): `Type Check UI` red. The job's `turbo run type-check --filter=...[<base>]` affected-scope is empty, so 0 tasks execute and nothing under `ui/packages/*/dist` is built; the next step `pnpm --dir ui run type-check:vitest-setup` (`tsc -p tsconfig.vitest-setup.json`) then fails with TS2882 / TS2307 on `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/fields`, `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard`, `@object-ui/plugin-grid`, `@object-ui/i18n/locales` — the packages whose `types` point at `dist/`.
- 4a #25745 head `fb110c2323` (changes `ui/` packages): the same job green — turbo built the affected packages first.
- #25852 (ui scripts change): see its run for the same shape. The red is a property of the diff, not of the tree.

## Wanted

1. In `ci.yml` `type-check-ui`: either build the packages `tsconfig.vitest-setup.json` resolves before the vitest-setup step (`turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/components --filter=@object-ui/fields --filter=@object-ui/plugin-dashboard --filter=@object-ui/plugin-grid --filter=@object-ui/i18n` with the turbo cache the job already restores), or make `type-check:vitest-setup` resolve those packages from source (`paths` in `ui/tsconfig.vitest-setup.json`) — the seat measures both and says which is cheaper per run; ⛔ do not skip the step or narrow the job's `if:`.
2. The job's own gate rosters follow (`check-ci-filter-parity`, `check-expected-skips`, `check-step-collectors`, `check-workflow-step-name-quoting`); each `--self-test` 0.
3. Prove it on this PR (which changes no `ui/` package, so the affected-scope is empty by construction): `Type Check UI` green here = the fix.

## Acceptance

- `Type Check UI` green on this PR and on a `ui/`-touching PR of the same day; the derived gate list for the diff exits 0.
- On the card: the per-run cost delta of the chosen fix (job duration before/after), so the maintainer can add the context to the required set (a separate settings step, after this merges; the registry row rides the same two-step as the step 6 card).

**Size:** S. **Clause-②:** no. **Metadata-protocol:** none.
